source_table: 'Case presentation' and 'Immune-mediated adverse events' sections with Fig. 1a,b and Fig. 2
notes: [clinical_programs] grade_provisional. 40-year-old woman with a likely pathogenic SOD1 variant (c.-358-10T>G), German early-access programme then approved use; dosing on days 1, 14 and 28 then 29 maintenance doses at a median 29-day interval, most recent March 2025. Progressively worsening prolonged holocephalic headache from the third dose; between the 20th and 23rd doses she had transient fever, shivering, fatigue and radiating leg pain after each intrathecal administration. Gradually increasing CSF pleocytosis and protein, new intrathecal IgM synthesis with a rising CSF/serum IgM ratio after the 7th dose, and spinal MRI before the 15th dose showing contrast enhancement of the caudal fibres and partial cervical-root involvement. Managed with intravenous methylprednisolone 1000 mg for 3 days at doses 15, 16 and 20 plus oral methotrexate 10 mg/week from dose 19 and 20 mg/week from dose 20; TOFERSEN WAS CONTINUED throughout -> reversible and manageable. Numeric CSF cell counts and protein values appear only in figures, so readout_value=TBD. ;; source_ref_as_cited=PMID:41144002; doi:10.1007/s00415-025-13415-3

notes: [nonclinical] grade_provisional; 7-week-old female C57BL/6 mice, n=4/group, single ICV injection of 15.2 nmol (100 ug). readout_value is TBD because Figure 1B is a grouped bar chart in which the two day-7 peaks (group means of roughly 9 and 6.5 on the 0-15 tolerability axis) and the smaller day-14 to day-21 bars (roughly 1.5-2.5) could not be assigned to individual ASOs with confidence from the colour key. Late-ONSET CNS toxicity: signs appeared at least 3 days after a single central injection, persisted for 6 days or more and worsened over time. The authors emphasise this is distinct from acute toxicity - no acute neurotoxicity was seen with ASO1, ASO3 or ASO4, and the acute toxicity of ASO2 resolved completely within 1 day. source_table: Figure 3B (NHP panel), group mean read from the bar chart
notes: [nonclinical] grade_provisional; adult male/female cynomolgus monkeys (2M/3F), 1 mL of ASO in aCSF by percutaneous lumbar (target L4/L5) intrathecal injection, dosed weekly with escalating doses of 4, 8, 12 and 16 mg. NHP acute-inhibition scale (Supplementary Fig. S1C): one point for absence of each of the tail, cutaneous, sensory-foot, proprioceptive and knee-jerk reflexes assessed 2-4 h after intrathecal dosing, summed per animal. Acute inhibition in NHP presents as loss of lower spinal reflexes 2-4 h post-dose. Group-mean 3-h acute inhibition score read off the published bar chart (approximate, +/-0.5 on the 0-7 axis); the paper reports per-group P values but not the numeric means. NOTE: Supplementary Table 10 tabulates the NHP dose column as 30/100/300/700 ug, which contradicts the figure and the main text (4, 8, 12 and 16 mg); the mg values from the figure and text are used here and the discrepancy is flagged. ;; source_ref_as_cited=doi:10.1093/nar/gkaf1333; PMID 41494985; PMC12865454

effect_vs_control: score 3.0 vs 0 in PBS-injected controls; full-PS vs mixed PS/PO comparison at this dose P = 0.0286 (Mann-Whitney, Supplementary Table 13)
source_table: Figure 5C (ASO5 panel), group mean read from the bar chart
notes: [nonclinical] grade_provisional; n=4 mice/group, single ICV bolus in PBS without Ca2+/Mg2+, scored 3 h post-dose. Group-mean 3-h acute inhibition score read off the published bar chart (approximate, +/-0.5 on the 0-7 axis); the paper reports per-group P values but not the numeric means. Rodent ICV acute-inhibition scale (Supplementary Fig. S1B): 0 bright/alert/responsive; 1 mild gait impairment; 2 obvious impaired gait/hunched posture; 3 moves away after lifting; 4 does not move forward but upright; 5 lying on side, responds to tail pinch; 6 no response to pinch but breathing; 7 death. Grade mapping for this 0-7 ICV scale: 0->0; 0<s<2->1; 2<=s<4->2; s>=4->3. Reducing PS content in the wings (six PS linkages replaced by PO) lowered the score for most but not all sequences (abolished for ASO2, no significant reduction for ASO8). ;; source_ref_as_cited=doi:10.1093/nar/gkaf1333; PMID 41494985; PMC12865454

source_table: Figure 1A (time-course dose response), statistics in Supplementary Table 3
notes: [nonclinical] grade_provisional; n>=11 male rats (281 +/- 9 g), single IT bolus in 30 uL, scored in 15-min blocks over 120 min. Group means at these sub-threshold doses overlap the vehicle band and were not digitised, hence readout_value TBD. Acute neuronal activation (aA) response: shaking, muscle twitching, cramping, hyperactivity, hyperreactivity, vocalisation, tremors, convulsions and seizures, peaking ~15 min after intrathecal dosing and resolving by ~120 min with no apparent sequelae. Scored 0-7 (7 = requires euthanasia). Score >=5 is defined by the authors as severe (vocalisation and/or seizures). ;; source_ref_as_cited=doi:10.1093/nar/gkag057; PMID 41633500; PMC12867516
